miller.title: Evan Miller (2024), Adding Error Bars to Evals, §§2–5
miller.claims: Verified: task-level differences for paired comparisons; clustered questions require dependence-aware uncertainty; averaging repeated answers reduces within-question variability; sample-size planning uses effect and variance assumptions.

wilson.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, §7.2.4.1: Confidence intervals for proportions
wilson.claims: Verified: Wilson formula, bounded endpoints, distinction from the Wald interval, and exact binomial interval construction.

mean.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, §1.3.5.2: Confidence limits for the mean
mean.claims: Verified: mean interval uses standard deviation divided by square root of sample size and a t critical value; interpretation concerns repeated interval construction.

paired.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, §7.3.1.1: Analysis of paired observations
paired.claims: Verified: form within-pair differences and analyze their mean; the paired t procedure uses the variance of those differences.

bootstrap.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.bootstrap
bootstrap.claims: Verified: resampling with replacement, percentile/basic/BCa alternatives, paired=True shares sampled indices, and degenerate distributions need care. The local lab explicitly uses percentile intervals, not the SciPy default.

asa.title: American Statistical Association (2016), Statement on statistical significance and p-values: release and six principles
asa.claims: Verified: p-values do not give hypothesis probabilities or effect importance; threshold-only decisions and selective reporting are inappropriate.

binomial.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.binomtest
binomial.claims: Verified: test of a binomial success probability with two-sided and one-sided alternatives. The local discordance test specializes the binomial null to p=0.5.

bonferroni.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, §7.4.6.3: Bonferroni’s method
bonferroni.claims: Verified: allocating alpha across a specified family bounds its overall error using the Bonferroni inequality.

sequential.title: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe & Sekhon, Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
sequential.claims: Verified from abstract: confidence sequences provide time-uniform coverage under their assumptions. No particular implementation or sample efficiency is claimed in the course.

metrics.title: scikit-learn user guide, §3.4: Metrics and scoring
metrics.claims: Verified: confusion-matrix and precision/recall/F-score definitions; averaging schemes change what summary metrics mean. The examples and confusion matrices here are original.

calibration.title: scikit-learn user guide, §1.16: Probability calibration
calibration.claims: Verified: reliability diagrams compare forecast averages with observed frequencies; proper scores assess more than calibration alone; calibration fitting requires independent data.

beta.title: Joram Soch, The Book of Statistical Proofs: Posterior distribution for binomial observations
beta.claims: Verified: Beta prior with Binomial likelihood yields Beta(alpha+successes, beta+failures). Course posterior numbers are computed locally.

blocks.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, §5.3.3.2: Randomized block designs
blocks.claims: Verified: blocking controls known nuisance factors and randomization operates within blocks. Application to agent execution order is an original course design example.

humaneval.title: Chen et al. (2021), Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code, §2.1
humaneval.claims: Verified: pass@k estimates whether at least one of k samples passes and uses 1-C(n-c,k)/C(n,k). No model performance claims are reproduced.

equivalence.title: statsmodels documentation: paired two-one-sided equivalence tests
equivalence.claims: Verified: equivalence is tested against specified lower and upper limits using two one-sided tests; it is not established by failing to reject a zero difference.

agreement.title: scikit-learn documentation: Cohen’s kappa
agreement.claims: Verified: kappa=(observed agreement−expected agreement)/(1−expected agreement), with expected agreement derived from empirical label marginals; weighting options for ordinal labels.

fdr.title: statsmodels documentation: multiple-test corrections
fdr.claims: Verified: implementations distinguish FWER and FDR procedures, including Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini–Hochberg, and Benjamini–Yekutieli; dependence assumptions matter.

bh1995.title: Benjamini & Hochberg (1995), Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing, JRSS-B 57(1), 289–300
bh1995.claims: Verified from Crossref metadata only: title, authors, journal, volume, issue, pages, year, and DOI. The publisher page refused the fetch and the only PDF located was a scanned image, so the full text was not read. The FDR definition and the step-up rule used in the course are taken from the SciPy and statsmodels documentation that cite this paper.

fdr-scipy.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.false_discovery_control
fdr-scipy.claims: Verified: the false discovery rate is the expected proportion of rejected null hypotheses that are actually true; the Benjamini–Hochberg method is for independent tests or positive regression dependence and Benjamini–Yekutieli for arbitrary dependence; references Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) 57.1:289–300 and Benjamini & Yekutieli (2001).

pearson.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.pearsonr
pearson.claims: Verified: the coefficient is the summed cross-product of deviations from the means divided by the root of the product of the summed squared deviations; range −1 to +1; the default p-value assumes uncorrelated normally distributed data; method=PermutationMethod computes the p-value with permutation_test instead.

spearman.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.spearmanr
spearman.claims: Verified: a nonparametric measure of the monotonicity of a relationship, range −1 to +1 with ±1 an exact monotone relation; its analytic p-value is only accurate for very large samples and a permutation test is recommended otherwise; a constant input makes the coefficient undefined.

permutation.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.permutation_test
permutation.claims: Verified: the pairings permutation type re-pairs observations within samples and is appropriate for correlation tests; for randomized tests the numerator and denominator of the p-value are both increased by one and the observed statistic is included in the null distribution; the exact null distribution is computed when the resample count is at least the number of distinct permutations.

holdout.title: scikit-learn user guide, §3.1: Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance
holdout.claims: Verified: fitting and testing on the same data is a methodological mistake (overfitting); tuning settings against a test set lets knowledge of it leak into the evaluation, so a separate validation set is held out and the test set is used once at the end.

neuron-explainer.title: OpenAI automated-interpretability repository: neuron_explainer/explanations/scoring.py
neuron-explainer.claims: Verified in the released code: correlation_score returns np.corrcoef(real_activations, predicted_activations)[0, 1], and the aggregate score computes that correlation over all activations rather than averaging per-sequence correlations. The accompanying paper page rendered only its table of contents, so no claim from the paper text is reproduced here.
